AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 7c1acb6c9194 Provenance

Provides an efficient, non-owning read view of contiguous character sequences without memory allocation.

ara::core::StringView provides a non-owning, read-only view of contiguous character sequences of type char ([SWS_CORE_02100]). It allows efficient text checks, searches, and substring generations without dynamic memory allocation ([SWS_CORE_02141]). All functions are declared noexcept; range violations trigger an IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation or, in the case of unprotected accesses, undefined behavior.

Context

The class ara::core::StringView provides an implementation of the standard type std::basic_string_view from [string.view] in the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. According to [SWS_CORE_02100], it is fixedly specialized for the character type char (value_type = char). As a constant, non-owning reference, it encapsulates contiguous character storage via a pointer ([SWS_CORE_02102]) and a length specification ([SWS_CORE_02109]). The class primarily serves as an efficient parameter for interfaces to transmit and inspect text data in a read-only manner without dynamic memory allocations or copy operations.

For read access, the class defines standard-compliant alias types such as const_pointer ([SWS_CORE_02102]), const_reference ([SWS_CORE_02104]), difference_type ([SWS_CORE_02110]) as well as bidirectional iterators (iterator, const_iterator according to [SWS_CORE_02105] and [SWS_CORE_02106] as well as reverse iterators according to [SWS_CORE_02107] and [SWS_CORE_02108]). Invalid positions are signaled via the static constant npos ([SWS_CORE_02111]).

Lifecycle

Instances of ara::core::StringView can be created as empty views ([SWS_CORE_02112]), from null-terminated C strings ([SWS_CORE_02113]), or from a pointer with an explicit length specification ([SWS_CORE_02114]). All constructors are declared as constexpr and noexcept. The lifecycle of the view is strictly decoupled from that of the underlying memory: StringView assumes no ownership of the data. The destructor is recorded as a defaulted operation ([SWS_CORE_02119]) and does not release the memory.

The copy constructor ([SWS_CORE_02115]) and assignment operator ([SWS_CORE_02116]) are defined as default. In addition to the C++17 standard, AUTOSAR explicitly also specifies the move constructor ([SWS_CORE_02117]) and move assignment ([SWS_CORE_02118]) as noexcept = default. Two views can be swapped efficiently via swap() ([SWS_CORE_02139]). With regard to concurrency, read access to the same instance from multiple threads is likely to be thread-safe because all read operations are const; modifying calls, on the other hand, require external synchronization.

Usage Path

A typical workflow includes instantiation, validation, pattern searching, and extraction of subranges:

  • Initialization and size check: After creation from a buffer ([SWS_CORE_02114]), the state is determined via empty() ([SWS_CORE_02131]), size() ([SWS_CORE_02128]), or data() ([SWS_CORE_02136]).
  • Prefix and content check: The presence of fixed patterns can be checked efficiently without copying by means of starts_with() ([SWS_CORE_02148]–[SWS_CORE_02150]), ends_with() ([SWS_CORE_02151]–[SWS_CORE_02153]), or contains() ([SWS_CORE_02154]–[SWS_CORE_02156]).
  • Search and decomposition: Delimiters are located via find() ([SWS_CORE_02157]–[SWS_CORE_02160]), rfind() ([SWS_CORE_02161]–[SWS_CORE_02164]), or character set search functions such as find_first_of() ([SWS_CORE_02165]–[SWS_CORE_02168]). By means of substr() ([SWS_CORE_02141]) or remove_prefix() ([SWS_CORE_02137]) or remove_suffix() ([SWS_CORE_02138]), the viewing window is narrowed down to relevant subsections.
  • Comparison and copy: By means of compare() ([SWS_CORE_02142]–[SWS_CORE_02147]), lexicographical comparisons can be made, and character sequences can be transferred to external buffers via copy() ([SWS_CORE_02140]).

Sequence diagram: Typical call sequence for inspection and substring generation without memory allocation. Sources: [SWS_CORE_02114], [SWS_CORE_02148], [SWS_CORE_02158], [SWS_CORE_02141], [SWS_CORE_02131]

Error Scenarios

All functions of the class are declared as noexcept. Deviations from the ISO C++ standard concern the handling of range violations: instead of throwing exceptions of type std::out_of_range, an IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered upon position overruns. This applies to:

  • at(pos) if pos >= size() ([SWS_CORE_02133]),
  • substr(pos, n) if pos > size() ([SWS_CORE_02141]),
  • copy(s, n, pos) if pos > size() ([SWS_CORE_02140]),
  • Overloads of compare() if pos1 > size() or pos2 > s.size() ([SWS_CORE_02143], [SWS_CORE_02144], [SWS_CORE_02146], [SWS_CORE_02147]).

Some functions have preconditions whose violation leads to undefined behavior: The index operator operator[](pos) does not check bounds and leads to undefined behavior if pos >= size() ([SWS_CORE_02132]). Likewise, calling front() ([SWS_CORE_02134]) or back() ([SWS_CORE_02135]) on empty instances (empty() == true) leads to undefined behavior. If more characters are removed with remove_prefix(n) ([SWS_CORE_02137]) or remove_suffix(n) ([SWS_CORE_02138]) than the view contains (n > size()), the behavior is also undefined. In addition, an StringView surviving past the end of the lifetime of the referenced character storage leads to dangling pointers; the class presumably does not perform any runtime check of pointer validity.

This text was created and curated by an AI. All statements are substantiated by the AUTOSAR specification R25-11.

                      function at [SWS_CORE_02133]
                      

                      constexpr const_reference at (size_type pos) const noexcept;
                      

                      As per corresponding usage in [string.view] except for the following deviations: 1. The function is noexcept 2. if (pos >= size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                      

                      

                      

                      

                      

                      

                      

                      

                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b7697f8c19b0
  Provenance
  

                      

                      

                      use
                      

                      The member function at of class ara::core::StringView provides synchronous read access to individual characters ([SWS_CORE_02133]). It accepts as parameter the index pos of type size_type and returns a const reference (const_reference) to the character at this position. The function is specified as constexpr and noexcept, which also allows calls to be evaluated at compile time.
                      


                      Error handling
                      

                      Contrary to the behavior in standard [string.view], the function does not throw an exception of type std::out_of_range in case of error ([SWS_CORE_02133]). If condition pos >= size() is fulfilled, a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered instead. The specification classifies the function as exception safe (exception safe).
                      


                      Concurrency and Limitations
                      

                      Since at is declared as const, the call does not modify the underlying instance. The caller must ensure that the referenced string remains valid for the entire lifetime of the StringView object. When out-of-bounds violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation occurs, execution is likely terminated in a controlled manner; user-defined abort routines can be registered for this via AddAbortHandler ([SWS_CORE_00054]) (Interpretation).
                      


                      Interaction
                      

                      The concept of intercepting out-of-bounds accesses via IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is applied consistently across multiple containers in ara::core:
                      

                        

                      • In ara::core::Array ([SWS_CORE_01273], [SWS_CORE_01274]) and ara::core::Map ([SWS_CORE_01456], [SWS_CORE_01457]), at is likewise declared as noexcept and exception safe.
                        • 

                      • In contrast, the corresponding at functions in ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01354], [SWS_CORE_01355]) as well as in ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03063], [SWS_CORE_03064]) are classified as not exception safe (not exception safe) and not marked as noexcept.
                        •

                                          use
                                          

                                          
The member function compare of class ara::core::StringView from header #include "ara/core/string_view.h" serves for the synchronous lexicographical comparison of the current string view with a passed instance s of type StringView [SWS_CORE_02142]. The behavior is based on the corresponding usage in [string.view] of the C++ standard [SWS_CORE_02142]. As a return value, the function provides an int, which represents the relational relationship of the character sequences [SWS_CORE_02142].

                                          

                                          Error handling
                                          

                                          
The function is declared with noexcept and specified as exception safe [SWS_CORE_02142]. It does not throw C++ exceptions. Specific error codes, AUTOSAR development errors (DET), or notifications to the Diagnostic Event Manager (DEM) are not provided for this operation [SWS_CORE_02142].

                                          

                                          Concurrency and Constraints
                                          

                                          
Due to the classification as const and constexpr, the call can already be evaluated at compile time [SWS_CORE_02142]. Interpretation: Since the function accesses immutable character sequences in a read-only manner, a concurrent call via the same StringView from multiple threads is expected to be thread-safe, provided that the underlying character data is not modified.

                                          

                                          Interaction
                                          

                                          
While basic types in ara::core such as ErrorDomain [SWS_CORE_00137] or ErrorCode [SWS_CORE_00571] primarily provide binary equality operators for checks, compare in StringView offers a three-way comparison value [SWS_CORE_02142].

                                              use
                                              

                                              The member function compare of class ara::core::StringView performs a synchronous lexicographical comparison of a substring of the current string view with a passed StringView s [SWS_CORE_02143]. The substring to be compared begins at index pos1 and encompasses a length of at most n1 characters. The return value is an integer int indicating the relational result. Since the function is declared as constexpr, evaluation can already take place at compile time [SWS_CORE_02143].
                                              

                                              Error handling
                                              

                                              The semantics are based on the requirements of [string.view] from the ISO C++ standard, but define two major deviations [SWS_CORE_02143]:
                                              

                                                

                                              • The function is specified with noexcept and is considered exception safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02143].
                                                • 

                                              • If the start index exceeds the length of the view (pos1 > size()), no standard exception of type std::out_of_range is thrown, but a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is caused [SWS_CORE_02143].
                                                • 

                                              

                                              Concurrency and Constraints
                                              

                                              Callers must ensure in advance that pos1 does not exceed the value of size() in order to avoid a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation [SWS_CORE_02143]. Since compare is declared as const and performs no modifications to the instance, concurrent read access from multiple threads is expected to be non-critical (interpretation).

                                                  The member function compare of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02144], header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h") serves for the synchronous, lexicographical comparison of two substrings. The fundamental behavior corresponds to the functionality in [string.view] of the ISO C++ standard, but exhibits specific deviations for AUTOSAR Adaptive [SWS_CORE_02144].
                                                  


                                                  The passed parameters determine the sections of both sequences to be compared [SWS_CORE_02144]:
                                                  

                                                    

                                                  • pos1 and n1: Start index and maximum character count within the calling instance.
                                                    • 

                                                  • s: The object of type StringView to be compared.
                                                    • 

                                                  • pos2 and n2: Start index and maximum character count within the passed object s.
                                                    • 

                                                  


                                                  As a return value, the function delivers an integer value (int) that is negative if the own subsequence is lexicographically smaller, zero upon match, and positive if it is greater [SWS_CORE_02144].
                                                  


                                                  Regarding error handling, the implementation deviates from the standard: The method is declared as noexcept and is considered exception safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02144]. If one of the start positions lies outside the valid range (pos1 > size() || pos2 > s.size()), no std::out_of_range exception is thrown, but a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised [SWS_CORE_02144].
                                                  


                                                  Due to the qualifiers constexpr and const, the function can already be evaluated during compilation [SWS_CORE_02144]. Since no internal states are modified, concurrent read accesses to the same instance are expected to be thread-safe.

                                                      The member function compare of class ara::core::StringView (header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h") serves the synchronous, lexicographical comparison of the current string view with a null-terminated C string const char* s [SWS_CORE_02145]. Since the operation is specified as constexpr, evaluation can take place both at runtime and within the context of compile-time expressions. As a return value, the function returns an integer value of type int whose sign reflects the comparison result analogously to [string.view]: a value less than zero means that the instance precedes s lexicographically; the value zero means equality; a value greater than zero indicates that the instance succeeds s [SWS_CORE_02145].
                                                      

                                                      Regarding error handling, the AUTOSAR specification explicitly deviates from the template in [string.view]: The method is declared as noexcept and has the property exception safe [SWS_CORE_02145]. Calls are thus guaranteed not to throw C++ exceptions. Specific error codes, feedback to the Development Error Tracer (DET) or the Diagnostic Event Manager (DEM) are not provided for this basic function.
                                                      

                                                      As a const-qualified method, compare does not modify the state of the ara::core::StringView instance and can be called safely for concurrent reading. When using it, it should be noted that the pointer s presumably must refer to a valid character sequence, since the semantics adopted from [string.view] would likely result in undefined behavior if a null pointer is passed [SWS_CORE_02145].

                                                          use
                                                          

                                                          The method compare of class ara::core::StringView enables a synchronous lexicographical comparison of a substring of the string view with a null-terminated C string s [SWS_CORE_02146]. Passed are the start index pos1, the maximum length n1, and the pointer s to the character sequence to be compared. The return value of type int reflects the relational ordering result analogously to the standard library: a return value less than zero, equal to zero, or greater than zero characterizes the lexicographical relationship [SWS_CORE_02146].
                                                          


                                                          Error Handling and Boundary Conditions
                                                          

                                                          The operation is specified as noexcept and \"exception safe\" [SWS_CORE_02146]. In contrast to the behavior according to C++ standard [string.view], an invalid start index with pos1 > size() does not trigger a std::out_of_range exception, but leads to a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation [SWS_CORE_02146]. In the AUTOSAR runtime context, this violation is expected to be treated as a programming error and force an immediate platform abort, since regular C++ exceptions cannot escape across noexcept boundaries. Furthermore, it must be ensured that s refers to a valid string, since a null pointer presumably causes undefined behavior.
                                                          


                                                          Concurrency
                                                          

                                                          Since compare is defined as const and constexpr, the state of the instance remains unchanged [SWS_CORE_02146]. Concurrent read accesses to the same ara::core::StringView object can thus be executed safely.

                                                              Interpretation: Due to the combination of the noexcept guarantee and IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation, an out-of-bounds condition is not expected to be catchable by means of classic C++ try-catch blocks, but presumably leads to an immediate abort or error handling by the platform.

                                                                  Usage and Call Context
                                                                  

                                                                  
The member function contains of class ara::core::StringView serves for the synchronous check of whether a string view contains a specified substring [SWS_CORE_02154]. The function is defined in header ara/core/string_view.h according to the semantics of the C++ standard working draft N4950 ([string.view]) [SWS_CORE_02154]. As a parameter, the method takes another instance of StringView (sv) by value and directly returns a boolean value of type bool: true if the subsequence occurs, otherwise false [SWS_CORE_02154].

                                                                  

                                                                  
Due to the specification as constexpr, the call can take place both at runtime and already during translation in the context of compile-time contexts [SWS_CORE_02154].

                                                                  


                                                                  Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                  

                                                                  
For contains, the behavior is stipulated as exception safe and the signature is explicitly designated with noexcept [SWS_CORE_02154]. Consequently, the function never throws C++ exceptions under any circumstances and does not return errors via ara::core::Result or ara::core::ErrorCode. Neither DET nor DEM error messages exist for this basic function.

                                                                  


                                                                  Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                  

                                                                  
As a const member function (const), contains does not modify the state of the StringView instance [SWS_CORE_02154]. Interpretation: Concurrent, purely reading calls on the same StringView instance or on the underlying character buffer are expected to be fully reentrant and concurrently safe, as long as the referenced memory area is not modified simultaneously by any thread. Special ordering conditions or initialization obligations beyond the provision of a valid StringView do not exist.

                                                                      The member function contains synchronously checks whether a specific character c is contained within a ara::core::StringView [SWS_CORE_02155]. The function is declared in header ara/core/string_view.h and follows the semantics of [string.view] from the C++ working draft N4950 [SWS_CORE_02155]. It accepts a single character of type char and returns a boolean value of type bool, which presumably yields true if and only if the character is found in the referenced text range [SWS_CORE_02155].
                                                                      

                                                                      Regarding error handling, the operation is declared as noexcept and specified as exception-safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02155]. No exceptions are thrown and no error codes are signaled via DET, DEM, or return types; non-existence of the character is regularly reported via the boolean return value.

Invocations do not modify the underlying ara::core::StringView object, which is why concurrent read accesses to the same instance should presumably be thread-safe.
                                                                      

                                                                      In the interplay of basic types of the module core, contains serves for direct text inspection on string views [SWS_CORE_02155]. While types like ara::core::Result offer their own check mechanisms for contained values or errors – such as HasValue [SWS_CORE_00751] or CheckError [SWS_CORE_00765] –, contains operates lightweight without allocation or error encapsulation.

                                                                              function copy [SWS_CORE_02140]
                                                                              

                                                                              size_type copy (char *s, size_type n, size_type pos=0) const noexcept;
                                                                              

                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [string.view] except for the following deviations: 1. The function is noexcept 2. if (pos > size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 63860f6d57ee
  Provenance
  

                                                                              

                                                                              

                                                                              use
                                                                              

                                                                              The synchronous member function copy of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02140]) copies a substring into a provided buffer. Access is provided via header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h":
                                                                              

                                                                                

                                                                              • Parameters: char *s points to the destination array, n determines the maximum number of characters to copy, and pos defines the starting position (default value 0).
                                                                                • 

                                                                              • Return value: A value of type size_type indicating the number of characters actually copied.
                                                                                • 

                                                                              • Semantics: The function operates synchronously and is aligned with the ISO C++ specification [string.view] ([SWS_CORE_02140]).
                                                                                • 

                                                                              


                                                                              Error handling
                                                                              

                                                                              In case of an error, when pos > size() holds, an IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised ([SWS_CORE_02140]). This deviates from standard [string.view], which throws std::out_of_range. Since the interface is declared as noexcept, raising the violation presumably leads to immediate termination of the process (interpretation: no C++ exception is propagated).
                                                                              


                                                                              Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                              

                                                                              The operation is specified as const as well as noexcept and is considered exception safe ([SWS_CORE_02140]). The caller must ensure that the destination array s provides sufficient memory for at least min(n, size() - pos) characters, as range errors of the destination buffer are not caught.
                                                                              


                                                                              Interaction
                                                                              

                                                                              Compared to ara::core::BasicString::copy ([SWS_CORE_03410]), which works with value_type and is classified as not exception safe, the variant in StringView provides an exception-safe noexcept guarantee ([SWS_CORE_02140]).

                                                                                  function crbegin [SWS_CORE_02126]
                                                                                  

                                                                                  constexpr const_reverse_iterator crbegin () const noexcept;
                                                                                  

                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [string.view]
                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 231dd0a8e66b
  Provenance
  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  

                                                                                  The member function crbegin of class ara::core::StringView synchronously returns a constant reverse iterator (const_reverse_iterator) to the first character of the reversed string view [SWS_CORE_02126]. The function takes no parameters, is declared via header file ara/core/string_view.h, and follows the standard semantics of [string.view] [SWS_CORE_02126].
                                                                                  

                                                                                  Regarding error handling, the operation is defined as noexcept and specified as exception safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02126]. Neither error codes are returned nor error messages via DET or DEM issued, since the call is guaranteed to execute without errors [SWS_CORE_02126].
                                                                                  

                                                                                  Thanks to the specification as constexpr and const, the function can also be called within constant expressions at compile time [SWS_CORE_02126]. Interpretation: Parallel calls of crbegin on the same instance should be concurrently thread-safe, since the operation makes no modifications whatsoever to the object.
                                                                                  

                                                                                  The interface fits seamlessly into the cross-container iterator concept of AUTOSAR Adaptive Core. Equivalent constexpr implementations of crbegin are found in ara::core::Array [SWS_CORE_01260] as well as ara::core::Span [SWS_CORE_01978]. Furthermore, containers such as ara::core::Vector [SWS_CORE_01342], ara::core::Map [SWS_CORE_01450], and ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03049] also provide corresponding non-constexpr const_reverse_iterator entry points.

    The member function crend of class ara::core::StringView returns a constant reverse iterator ([SWS_CORE_02127]). The call executes synchronously and without parameters on an existing instance from header ara/core/string_view.h. The returned const_reverse_iterator marks the logical end of a reverse iteration; according to the C++ reference [string.view], it points as a sentinel position to the theoretical element immediately preceding the first character of the string (interpretation: analogous to the C++ standard).
  
                                                                                      
  
                                                                                      Error Handling and Concurrency
                                                                                      
  
                                                                                      
    The function is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (“exception safe”) ([SWS_CORE_02127]). Neither exceptions are thrown nor error codes returned or DET/DEM messages issued. Due to the constexpr qualification, the iterator can already be created at compile time. As a pure const method without state effects, concurrent read calls on the same instance should be concurrently safe (interpretation).
  
                                                                                      
  
                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                      
  
                                                                                      
    The interface follows the uniform iteration concept of ara::core for sequential data structures. Related specifications define analogous crend interfaces:

                                                                                        •

                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                      

                                                                                                      The member function ara::core::StringView::ends_with synchronously checks whether the inspected character sequence ends with the passed subsequence sv [SWS_CORE_02151]. It is declared in the header file ara/core/string_view.h and follows the standardized C++ semantics according to [string.view] from ISO/IEC 14882:2020 [SWS_CORE_02151]. Thanks to being marked as constexpr, the comparison can already be evaluated at compile time. Because this is a const method, the calling object is not modified.
                                                                                                      


                                                                                                      Error Handling and Concurrency

The function is noexcept

                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              The synchronous member function find of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02160]) from header #include "ara/core/string_view.h" searches for the first occurrence of the specified C string s starting from the start position pos. The functional behavior complies with the C++ standard [string.view], but deviates by being explicitly designated as noexcept ([SWS_CORE_02160]).
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Error handling
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              The function is defined as exception safe and guarantees the absence of any exceptions ([SWS_CORE_02160]). Specific error codes as well as reports to DET or DEM do not exist. Interpretation: If the searched string is not contained, the failure of the search is likely to be indicated by the return value npos analogously to the standard behavior of [string.view].
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Concurrency and Constraints
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Since find is declared as constexpr and const ([SWS_CORE_02160]), the call does not modify the state of the StringView object and can already be evaluated at compile time. Interpretation: Concurrent read accesses across multiple threads are likely to be reentrant and concurrency-safe without additional synchronization measures.
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                              Within ara::core::StringView, further overloads of find exist for StringView parameters ([SWS_CORE_02157]), single characters ([SWS_CORE_02158]), and substrings with an explicit length limitation n ([SWS_CORE_02159]). In contrast to analogous C-string search operations in ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03408], [SWS_CORE_03409]), which are classified as not exception safe, the implementation in ara::core::StringView ensures complete exception safety ([SWS_CORE_02160]).

                                                                                                                                  use
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  The member function find_first_not_of of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02173]) serves for synchronously searching for the first character within the string view that is not contained in the passed StringView s. As a second parameter, the start position pos can optionally be specified (default value pos=0). The function returns the found index position as size_type. The behavior complies with the corresponding semantics in [string.view]. Interpretation: If no non-matching character is found, the function is likely to return the value npos in accordance with this standard semantics.
                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Concurrency
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  The function is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (“exception safe”) ([SWS_CORE_02173]). No exceptions are thrown and no specific error reports via DET or DEM are defined. Due to the qualifiers const and constexpr, the call can take place side-effect-free at compile time or in parallel on unmodified objects.
                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                  Interplay and overloads
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  Within ara::core::StringView, the function is complemented by further noexcept overloads:
                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                  • Search for characters not equal to a single character char c ([SWS_CORE_02174]).
                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                  • Search based on a C string const char *s with length limitation n ([SWS_CORE_02175]) or starting from start position ([SWS_CORE_02176]).
                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                  A similar search pattern exists for ara::core::BasicString, including with StringView ([SWS_CORE_03319]) and BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03337]). In contrast to StringView, the overloads there for pointers and characters ([SWS_CORE_03338], [SWS_CORE_03339], [SWS_CORE_03340]) are classified as not exception safe.

                                                                                                                                      function find_first_not_of [SWS_CORE_02174]
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      constexpr size_type find_first_not_of (char c, size_type pos=0) const noexcept;
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [string.view]
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      
  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d93e1265f673
  Provenance
  

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      The member function find_first_not_of of class ara::core::StringView synchronously determines the position of the first character within the character sequence that is not equal to the passed character c [SWS_CORE_02174]. The search starts by default at the beginning of the view or from the optional offset pos. By referencing standard [string.view], the function presumably returns the zero-based index of type size_type of the found character or the value npos if no differing character exists.
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      With regard to error handling, the function is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe [SWS_CORE_02174]. It thus throws no exceptions, uses no DET or DEM messages, and reports the non-finding of a character purely via its return value.
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      As a constexpr and const method, find_first_not_of can already be evaluated at compile time and guarantees stateless, side-effect-free read access to the underlying character array. Concurrent calls on the same StringView instance are therefore reentrant and safe without additional synchronization.
                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                      The function is part of a family of search operations in ara::core::StringView and complements the overloads for searching for differing subsequences via StringView [SWS_CORE_02173] as well as pointer-length pairs or null-terminated C strings [SWS_CORE_02175] [SWS_CORE_02176]. A functional equivalent for mutable strings exists in ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03340], which, in contrast to StringView, is declared as not exception safe.

                                                                                                                                          The member function find_first_not_of of class ara::core::StringView serves according to [SWS_CORE_02175] to synchronously find the first character within the string that does not occur in a predefined character sequence. The behavior basically corresponds to the usage in [string.view] with the documented deviation that the function is declared as noexcept [SWS_CORE_02175]. Interpretation: Via the reference to [string.view], parameters s, pos, and n are likely to limit the search starting from position pos to the first n characters of array s [SWS_CORE_02175].
                                                                                                                                          

  
                                                                                                                                          Usage and Error Handling
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                          The function is defined as constexpr and const, is provided via the header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h", and returns an index of type size_type [SWS_CORE_02175]. The specification classifies the method as exception safe [SWS_CORE_02175]. Since it is specified as noexcept, it throws no exceptions; error codes or messages to DET or DEM are not defined [SWS_CORE_02175].
                                                                                                                                          

  
                                                                                                                                          Interaction and Alternatives
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                          In ara::core::StringView, related overloads are provided for different search patterns:
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                            
    
                                                                                                                                          • Search via another string view StringView according to [SWS_CORE_02173],
                                                                                                                                            • 
    
                                                                                                                                          • Search for the first deviation from a single character c according to [SWS_CORE_02174], and
                                                                                                                                            • 
    
                                                                                                                                          • Search using a null-terminated pointer const char *s without explicit length specification according to [SWS_CORE_02176].
                                                                                                                                            • 
  
                                                                                                                                          
  
                                                                                                                                          In contrast to the structurally similar signature in ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03338], which is classified as not exception safe and does not feature noexcept, the variant in StringView offers complete exception safety [SWS_CORE_02175].

The behavior corresponds to the definition in [string.view], but deviates by being explicitly designated as noexcept ([SWS_CORE_02176]). Interpretation: From the standard reference to [string.view], it likely follows that s must point to a valid, null-terminated character array and that npos is returned in case of failure.
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              Regarding error handling, the function is specified as exception safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_02176]). No exceptions are thrown; runtime error notifications via AUTOSAR mechanisms such as DET or DEM are not defined for this function in the payload.
                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                              Due to being qualified as constexpr and const ([SWS_CORE_02176]), the search operation does not modify the state of the StringView object.                                                                                                                                                       use
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      The member function find_first_of of class ara::core::StringView serves to synchronously search for the first occurrence of a character within the referenced string [SWS_CORE_02166]. It is available via the header ara/core/string_view.h and accepts the sought character c as well as optionally the start position pos, which is set to 0 by default. The function returns the index of the match of type size_type according to the behavior in [string.view] [SWS_CORE_02166]. As a constexpr method, it can be executed both at runtime and during compilation.
                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                      Error handling
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      The function is declared as noexcept and explicitly classified as “exception safe” [SWS_CORE_02166]. No exceptions are thrown, and the specification defines no specific error codes or reports to Development Error Tracer (DET) or Diagnostic Event Manager (DEM).
                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      As a const member function (const), calling it does not modify the instance of ara::core::StringView [SWS_CORE_02166]. Interpretation: Parallel, reading invocations on the same object from multiple threads are therefore likely to be reentrant and concurrently safe as long as the underlying character buffer remains unchanged.
                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                      The function is part of the search interfaces of ara::core::StringView. In addition to searching for single characters, analogous overloads, likewise specified as noexcept, exist for substrings via StringView [SWS_CORE_02165] as well as pointer representations [SWS_CORE_02167], [SWS_CORE_02168]. In contrast, class ara::core::BasicString declares related overloads for single characters [SWS_CORE_03332] and pointers [SWS_CORE_03330], [SWS_CORE_03331] without noexcept and classifies them as “not exception safe”, whereas the string variants with BasicString [SWS_CORE_03329] and StringView [SWS_CORE_03317] remain exception-safe.

                                                                                                                                                                  function find_last_not_of [SWS_CORE_02177]
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  constexpr size_type find_last_not_of (StringView s, size_type pos=0) const noexcept;

                                                                                                                                                                  The member function find_last_not_of of class ara::core::StringView serves for synchronously searching for the last character within the string that is not contained in the passed character sequence s ([SWS_CORE_02177]). The behavior complies with the C++ standard section [string.view] ([SWS_CORE_02177]). The function returns the found index position as size_type.
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding execution and safety, the method is characterized by the following properties:
                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                  • Compile time and exception safety: The function is declared as constexpr and noexcept and classified as “exception safe” ([SWS_CORE_02177]); error codes or error reports (such as DET/DEM) are not provided for this C++ helper type.
                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                  • Parameters and search position: pos=0 is stored as the start index in the signature ([SWS_CORE_02177]). Interpretation: Without an explicit specification of pos, the search is likely to take place backward from position 0, which is why callers typically have to pass a corresponding end position for a search over the entire string.
                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                  • Concurrency: Since it is a const member function (const), concurrent read access to the same StringView instance is possible without side effects.
                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                  In module core, find_last_not_of for ara::core::StringView is additionally overloaded for single characters char ([SWS_CORE_02178]) and for pointers to strings const char* ([SWS_CORE_02179], [SWS_CORE_02180]). A related search operation on ara::core::BasicString also exists for StringView parameters ([SWS_CORE_03320]).

                                                                                                                                                                      The function find_last_not_of of class ara::core::StringView searches a string view backward for the last character that does not match the passed character c [SWS_CORE_02178]. The function is declared as constexpr and noexcept and is executed synchronously. It returns the found position as size_type; the optional parameter pos determines the start position of the backward search and has the default value 0 [SWS_CORE_02178].
                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling, the operation is specified as exception safe (exception safe); specific AUTOSAR error codes or reports to DET or DEM are not provided for this element [SWS_CORE_02178]. Since it is a stateless const member function on an immutable view, concurrent read access to the same instance is likely thread-safe (interpretation).
                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                      Within ara::core::StringView, the function complements further overloads that enable searching based on another StringView [SWS_CORE_02177] or via pointers to strings [SWS_CORE_02179], [SWS_CORE_02180]. Corresponding search functions are also provided by class ara::core::BasicString, such as for searching for single characters [SWS_CORE_03344] or string views [SWS_CORE_03320], although those for character sequences are partly not designated as exception safe [SWS_CORE_03342].

                                                                                                                                                                          function find_last_not_of [SWS_CORE_02179]
                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                          constexpr size_type find_last_not_of (const char *s, size_type pos, size_type n) const noexcept;

                                                                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                          The member function find_last_not_of of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02179]) determines the last position of a character within the character view up to position pos that does not occur in the first n characters of the passed character array s. The behavior corresponds to the C++ standard reference [string.view] ([SWS_CORE_02179]). The function operates synchronously and returns an index of type size_type; if no differing character is found, an invalid index value such as npos will likely result following convention.
                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Concurrency
                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                          According to the specification, the function is declared as noexcept and classified as exception-safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_02179]). According to the payload, specific error codes, DET, or DEM reports do not exist. As a const and constexpr function, the call does not modify the state of the StringView object and is suitable for compile-time evaluations as well as concurrent read access to the same instance.
                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                          Interplay and overloads
                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                          The function is part of a group of other search functions of ara::core::StringView, including variants for searching for StringView objects ([SWS_CORE_02177]), single characters ([SWS_CORE_02178]), and null-terminated strings ([SWS_CORE_02180]). In contrast to the corresponding counterpart in ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03342]), which is not designated as exception safe, the StringView variant guarantees complete freedom from exceptions ([SWS_CORE_02179]).

                                                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                              The member function find_last_not_of of class ara::core::StringView synchronously searches for the last character within the character view that does not occur in the passed string s [SWS_CORE_02180]. The function is specified as constexpr and const and is provided via the header file ara/core/string_view.h [SWS_CORE_02180]. The call accepts the pointer s to the comparison characters as well as optionally the start position pos and returns the found position of type size_type [SWS_CORE_02180].
                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                              The function is declared as noexcept and defined as exception-safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02180]. No specific error codes are returned and no exceptions are thrown. Compared to the underlying specification [string.view], the explicit deviation consists in the guaranteed noexcept property [SWS_CORE_02180].
                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                              Interaction with related functions
                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                              Within ara::core::StringView, related overloads exist for the search:
                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                                                                              • with an instance of StringView [SWS_CORE_02177],
                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                              • with a single character char [SWS_CORE_02178],
                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                              • with an additional restriction to n characters [SWS_CORE_02179].
                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                              In the related class ara::core::BasicString, analogous search functions are available [SWS_CORE_03320], although pointer overloads there are deviantly classified as not exception-safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_03343].

A string view s and an optional start position pos, whose default value is defined as 0 according to the signature [SWS_CORE_02169], are passed as parameters. The return value is of type size_type and provides the index of the last matching character [SWS_CORE_02169].

Due to the qualification as constexpr, the evaluation can already take place at compile time [SWS_CORE_02169]. Since this is a pure read operation on an immutable view, the function is likely safe for concurrent read accesses without synchronization overhead.
