                                                                                                                                                                                  Within ara::core::StringView, further overloads of find_last_of exist that accept single characters char [SWS_CORE_02170] or C strings with length specification [SWS_CORE_02171] or null termination [SWS_CORE_02172].                                                                                                                                                                                       The member function find_last_of of class ara::core::StringView serves for synchronously finding the last occurrence of a single character [SWS_CORE_02170]. It is declared in header <ara/core/string_view.h> and specified as constexpr and noexcept [SWS_CORE_02170].
                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                      Usage and Semantics
                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                      The method searches the character view for the passed character c, with the search being performed backward starting from position pos [SWS_CORE_02170]. pos = 0 is stored as the default value in the function signature [SWS_CORE_02170]. According to the standard reference to [string.view], the call returns the zero-based index of the match; Interpretation: If the character is not found in the searched range, the method is likely to return StringView::npos.
                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Concurrency
                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                      The operation is declared as noexcept and is considered completely exception safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02170]. Specific error codes, AUTOSAR DET, or DEM reports do not exist. Since it is a non-modifying operation on an immutable view, it can be used without side effects in concurrent read scenarios or at compile time.
                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction with related overloads
                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                      Within ara::core::StringView, the function complements further overloads of find_last_of that accept search patterns as StringView [SWS_CORE_02169] or as C-string pointers [SWS_CORE_02171], [SWS_CORE_02172]. In contrast to the related class ara::core::BasicString, whose character-based variant [SWS_CORE_03336] is classified as not exception safe and uses pos = npos as default, this implementation guarantees strict exception safety.

                                                                                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function find_last_of of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02171]) serves for synchronously searching for the last occurrence of any character from a set of n characters pointed to by pointer s. The search is performed backward starting from position pos. The function is provided via the header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h" and, due to the declaration as constexpr, can also be executed in the context of compile-time evaluations.
                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                          Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          The function is explicitly declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_02171]). In the event of an error or if not found, no exceptions are thrown and no DET or DEM reports are generated; the behavior follows the semantics of [string.view].
                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                          Restrictions and Concurrency
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          As a const-qualified method, find_last_of does not modify the underlying StringView object. Interpretation: The caller presumably must ensure that pointer s points to at least n valid characters, since the specification does not define independent buffer checks.
                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                          Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                          The method complements the other overloads of find_last_of within ara::core::StringView, including the variants for StringView ([SWS_CORE_02169]), single characters ([SWS_CORE_02170]), and null-terminated strings ([SWS_CORE_02172]). In contrast to the overload in ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03334]), which is classified as not exception safe, the StringView implementation guarantees complete noexcept semantics.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function remove_prefix of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02137]) is provided via header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h". It has signature constexpr void remove_prefix (size_type n) noexcept; ([SWS_CORE_02137]). The function accepts parameter n of type size_type and does not return a value. The semantics correspond to the standard usage in [string.view], but deviate in that the function is declared as noexcept ([SWS_CORE_02137]). As an interpretation, the method is also expected to be evaluable at compile time thanks to the constexpr specification.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Restrictions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The function is specified as exception safe (exception safe) and throws no exceptions ([SWS_CORE_02137]). Specific error codes or notifications via DET or DEM are not defined. However, an essential restriction applies: The behavior of the function is undefined if n > size() is true ([SWS_CORE_02137]). Callers must ensure before execution that the number of characters to be removed does not exceed the current length of the string view. Further specifications regarding reentrancy or concurrency are not described in the standard.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The member function remove_suffix of class ara::core::StringView is provided via header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h" [SWS_CORE_02138]. It serves to shorten the character window referenced by the view at the right margin (suffix) by the specified number of n characters. The operation is executed synchronously directly on the calling instance without a return value (void) [SWS_CORE_02138]. Thanks to the designation as constexpr, the function can also be called at compile time in compile-time contexts [SWS_CORE_02138].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding error handling, exception safety, and constraints, the following specification requirements apply [SWS_CORE_02138]:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Exception safety and standard deviation: The semantics are generally based on the corresponding usage in [string.view] of the C++ standard, but exhibit as an explicit deviation that the function is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (exception safe) [SWS_CORE_02138]. It therefore never throws exceptions and reports no error codes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Undefined behavior with invalid parameter: The behavior of the function is explicitly specified as undefined if the passed parameter n is greater than the current length of the view (n > size()) [SWS_CORE_02138].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Caller responsibility: Since neither exception handling nor runtime checks are provided, it is entirely the responsibility of the calling code to ensure that precondition n <= size() is always met before the call is made.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    •

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function rfind [SWS_CORE_02161]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          constexpr size_type rfind (StringView s, size_type pos=0) const noexcept;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [string.view]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
The function rfind of class ara::core::StringView ([SWS_CORE_02161]) serves to synchronously find the last occurrence of a substring specified by the parameter s (type StringView). The search position is controlled via the parameter pos of type size_type with the default value 0. As return value, the method returns the found position as size_type. The semantics follow the specification in [string.view] ([SWS_CORE_02161]). The function is defined as constexpr and is included via the header file #include "ara/core/string_view.h" ([SWS_CORE_02161]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Error handling
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
The interface is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe ([SWS_CORE_02161]). No exceptions are thrown and no errors are reported via DET or DEM instances. If the subsequence is not found, signaling is performed via the return value according to [string.view].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
Since rfind is declared as const, the call does not modify the object. Interpretation: Concurrent, purely read access by multiple threads to the same StringView instance should therefore be thread-safe without external synchronization.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
Within ara::core::StringView, overloads exist for single characters ([SWS_CORE_02162]) as well as raw pointers with length specification ([SWS_CORE_02163]) or start position ([SWS_CORE_02164]), which are likewise designed as constexpr and noexcept. In addition, ara::core::BasicString provides corresponding rfind methods for passing StringView ([SWS_CORE_03316]) or string objects ([SWS_CORE_03325], [SWS_CORE_03326], [SWS_CORE_03327], [SWS_CORE_03328]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function rfind of class ara::core::StringView serves for backward searching of a single character within a string view [SWS_CORE_02162]. It is provided via header ara/core/string_view.h and follows the corresponding semantics in [string.view] [SWS_CORE_02162].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding invocation context and parameters:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Parameters: The function takes the searched character c of type char as well as optionally the start position pos of type size_type, whose default value according to the signature is 0 [SWS_CORE_02162].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Return value: The result is returned as a position index of type size_type [SWS_CORE_02162].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Execution: The call executes synchronously and is specified as constexpr and const, so that evaluation can also take place at compile time [SWS_CORE_02162].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Regarding exception handling and concurrency, the method is classified as noexcept and “exception safe” [SWS_CORE_02162]. Specific DET or DEM error messages are not defined. Since it is a side-effect-free read operation on ara::core::StringView, the function should be callable concurrently by multiple threads for reading.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              In interaction with related interfaces, the function complements the overloads for searching partial views StringView [SWS_CORE_02161] as well as C string pointers with length restriction [SWS_CORE_02163] or default offset [SWS_CORE_02164]. In contrast to ara::core::BasicString::rfind for individual characters [SWS_CORE_03328], which is classified as not exception safe and uses pos = npos as the default, the StringView implementation guarantees complete freedom from exceptions [SWS_CORE_02162].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Member function [SWS_CORE_02163] of class ara::core::StringView from header ara/core/string_view.h performs a synchronous backward search for a substring. It accepts a pointer s to the characters to be searched, a start position pos, and the character count n. The semantics correspond to the specification in [string.view], but deviate through the explicit specification as noexcept. Found positions are returned as a value of type size_type.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  For error handling, the specification provides that the function is exception safe (exception safe) and throws no exceptions [SWS_CORE_02163]. Error reports via DET or DEM as well as special error codes do not exist in the payload.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Since the operation is qualified with constexpr and const, it can already be evaluated at compile time [SWS_CORE_02163]. Interpretation: Multiple concurrent read accesses to the same StringView instance are expected to be executable thread-safely, since the method call does not modify the state of the object.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In the group of search functions, [SWS_CORE_02163] complements the related overloads for StringView objects [SWS_CORE_02161], single characters [SWS_CORE_02162], and pointers without length limitation [SWS_CORE_02164]. Compared to the pointer-based variant in ara::core::BasicString [SWS_CORE_03326], [SWS_CORE_02163] is characterized by guaranteed exception safety, whereas the string implementation is declared as not exception safe.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The synchronous member function rfind of class ara::core::StringView is used to find the last occurrence of a character string within a string view according to [SWS_CORE_02164]. The function is declared via header ara/core/string_view.h. It expects a pointer const char *s to the sought subsequence and optionally the start index size_type pos = 0 for the reverse search. The result is returned as size_type. Since the function is defined as constexpr, the search can be executed at runtime or already at compile time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      According to [SWS_CORE_02164], rfind is declared as noexcept and classified as exception safe (exception safe), which represents an explicit deviation from [string.view]. The throwing of C++ exceptions is thus excluded. Specific error codes as well as notifications to DEM or DET are not provided within the specification scope.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Since this is a const method, the call causes no modifying side effects on the ara::core::StringView object ([SWS_CORE_02164]). Interpretation: Due to the lack of an additional length parameter, the implementation is likely to expect that s points to a valid, null-terminated string.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Within ara::core::StringView, rfind is grouped with overloads for StringView arguments ([SWS_CORE_02161]), single characters ([SWS_CORE_02162]), and pointers with length specification n ([SWS_CORE_02163]). While class ara::core::BasicString offers comparable search operations (such as [SWS_CORE_03316]), pointer overloads there are partly not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_03327]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function starts_with of class ara::core::StringView synchronously checks whether the character sequence starts with the specified prefix sv of type StringView ([SWS_CORE_02148]). It is declared in header ara/core/string_view.h. As a constexpr method, the call can be evaluated both at runtime and at compile time. The semantics correspond to the specification of [string.view] from the C++20 standard ([SWS_CORE_02148]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error handling
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The function is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (“exception safe”) ([SWS_CORE_02148]). No exceptions are thrown and no error messages are issued via DET or DEM. If the character sequences do not match, false is regularly returned.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The specification provides no explicit details regarding thread safety. Interpretation: As a stateless const method on an immutable view, concurrent read access from multiple threads is likely to be safe and reentrant. No special call contexts or ordering constraints are specified.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              For the flexible checking of prefixes, two further overloads are available alongside the variant for StringView: one for individual characters char ([SWS_CORE_02149]) and one for null-terminated strings const char* ([SWS_CORE_02150]).

    The member function starts_with of class ara::core::StringView checks synchronously whether the character sequence starts with the passed single character c [SWS_CORE_02149]. The declaration is available via header ara/core/string_view.h and follows the behavior of [string.view] from the C++ standard ISO/IEC 14882:2020 [SWS_CORE_02149].
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Usage and Semantics
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    A single character of type char is passed as a parameter. The function returns a boolean value: true if the underlying string is not empty and its first character matches c, otherwise false. Due to the designation as constexpr, the comparison can already be evaluated at compile time [SWS_CORE_02149].
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    The specification designates the function as exception-safe (exception safe) and explicitly as noexcept [SWS_CORE_02149]. No exceptions are raised and no error codes are reported via DET or DEM. For an empty character sequence, no error occurs; instead, the function regularly returns false.
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Concurrency and Limitations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    Interpretation: Since this is a side-effect-free check function declared as const, concurrent read calls on the same StringView instance should be thread-safe. There are no specific sequencing constraints.
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
    The function complements the two other overloads of starts_with in ara::core::StringView:
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • the check against another character view starts_with(StringView sv) [SWS_CORE_02148], as well as
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • 
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • the check against a null-terminated string starts_with(const char *str) [SWS_CORE_02150].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The synchronous member function starts_with of class ara::core::StringView checks whether the referenced string starts with the null-terminated C string str ([SWS_CORE_02150]). The check result is returned as bool ([SWS_CORE_02150]). The function is defined as constexpr and is available via the header file ara/core/string_view.h ([SWS_CORE_02150]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Regarding error handling, the operation is declared as noexcept and specified as exception safe (exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_02150]). It accordingly throws no exceptions. Specific error codes, return values in case of error, or messages to DET or DEM are not provided for this function.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Because this is a const method, the call does not modify the StringView object ([SWS_CORE_02150]). Due to being marked as constexpr, evaluation can already take place at compile time ([SWS_CORE_02150]). Interpretation: The pointer str is likely to point to a valid character sequence and presumably must not be nullptr, as the semantics correspond to the C++ standard ISO/IEC 14882:2020 ([SWS_CORE_02150]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      In interplay with other interfaces, this overload complements two further variants of starts_with: checking based on a StringView object ([SWS_CORE_02148]) and based on a single character of type char ([SWS_CORE_02149]). All three overloads possess the same semantics according to [string.view] of the C++ standard and are exception safe ([SWS_CORE_02148], [SWS_CORE_02149], [SWS_CORE_02150]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function substr of class ara::core::StringView returns a subview of the underlying character range according to ISO C++ [string.view] [SWS_CORE_02141]. The function is provided via header #include "ara/core/string_view.h" and is declared as constexpr as well as noexcept [SWS_CORE_02141].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The parameters of the synchronous interface are defined as follows:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • pos: Starting position within the character view of type size_type with the default value 0 [SWS_CORE_02141].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • n: Maximum number of characters to take over of type size_type with the default value npos [SWS_CORE_02141].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          As a return value, a new StringView object referencing the specified character range is created [SWS_CORE_02141].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In case of an error, the specification provides for a deliberate deviation from the C++ standard: If pos > size() applies, violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std::out_of_range [SWS_CORE_02141]. Since substr is declared as exception safe and noexcept, triggering this violation is presumably implemented as a platform-wide violation handling mechanism and not as a thrown C++ exception [SWS_CORE_02141].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In interplay with ara::core::BasicString::substr [SWS_CORE_03345] from #include "ara/core/string.h", a functional difference appears: While BasicString::substr is classified as not exception safe and allocates a copied string, StringView::substr operates completely exception-safe and allocation-free [SWS_CORE_02141]. However, both functions handle out-of-range errors uniformly via IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation [SWS_CORE_02141] [SWS_CORE_03345].
